_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 2 Mathematics unit lecture film, Sides and Corners. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson opener's three parts (sides and corners; symmetry; turns) widened with the lesson page's own steps: step 1 counts sides and then corners by tapping, step 2 names a shape by its side count, step 6 is solid shapes and their faces, step 12 finds shapes in real things, step 5 judges a fold line, step 8 turns an arrow a quarter at a time and step 13 spins a square through a whole turn. Every number said here is drawn: the polygons are built from an explicit vertex count, and the cube's six faces, twelve edges and eight vertices are the picture library's own. Revised 2026-09-24 against two review notes: the solid chapter now also shows a FLAT familiar object (step 12's own door and clock face, alongside its dice, tin and ball), so 2Gg.08's '2D and 3D shapes in familiar objects' is not 3D alone; and the turn chapter now also turns anticlockwise (step 8's own arrow, from up to left), so 2Gg.11's 'both clockwise and anticlockwise' is not clockwise alone.
title: Sides and Corners
subtitle: Grade 2 Mathematics
objectives: Identify, describe, sort, name and sketch 2D shapes by their properties, including reference to regular polygons, number of sides and vertices. Recognise these shapes in different positions and orientations.
Identify, describe, sort and name 3D shapes by their properties, including reference to number and shapes of faces, edges and vertices.
Identify 2D and 3D shapes in familiar objects.
Identify a horizontal or vertical line of symmetry on 2D shapes and patterns.
Predict and check how many times a shape looks identical as it completes a full turn.
Understand that an angle is a description of a turn, including reference to the terms whole, half and quarter turns, both clockwise and anticlockwise.

beats.say: Every flat shape has sides and corners. Count them, and you can name it.
Solid shapes have faces and edges. Shapes fold, and shapes turn.
Here is a triangle. A side is one straight edge.
Go round in order, and count each side once: one, two, three.
A corner is the point where two sides meet.
Count the corners the same way, going round: one, two, three.
Now try a bigger shape. Count round the pentagon: five sides.
It has five corners too. Every side ends at a corner.
Counting the sides tells you the shape's name.
Three sides make a triangle. Four make a square or a rectangle.
Five sides make a pentagon. Six sides make a hexagon.
A shape turned round is still the same shape. A tipped square is still a square.
A face is a flat part you could paint. Every face of a cube is a square.
Count the faces of the cube: one, two, three, four, five, six.
The line where two faces meet is an edge. A cube has twelve.
A cube has eight corners as well. A dice is a cube.
A tin of beans is a cylinder. A ball is a sphere, curved all over.
A door is a flat shape: a rectangle. A clock face is a flat shape: a circle.
A line of symmetry is a fold line. Both halves match exactly.
Fold this square down the middle. The halves land on each other.
A rectangle folds across the middle as well. That works too.
A slanted fold does not work. The halves are not the same shape.
A turn can be a quarter turn, a half turn or a whole turn.
Clockwise means the way the hands of a clock go round.
This arrow points up. Turn it a quarter turn clockwise.
Now it points right. Another quarter, and it points down.
Two quarter turns make a half turn. A whole turn comes back to the start.
Anticlockwise is the other way round. A quarter turn from up points left.
Turn a square slowly all the way round. It looks the same four times.
One for each equal corner. Count the last one, back at the start.
Count the sides and the corners. The numbers always match.
Count its sides to name it: three, four, five, six.
Solid shapes have faces, edges and corners you can count.
A fold line makes matching halves. A whole turn comes back to the start.
